anf_compare.notes: Translated from the PG 74 Greek; no published English version was used for wording.

bible_refs.note: πῶς οὐχὶ καὶ σὺν αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα ἡμῖν χαριεῖται (NT χαρίσεται) closes the comment on the Romans 8:31–32 lemma begun in u07-rem-mid.
New lemma: τίς ἐγκαλέσει κατὰ ἐκλεκτῶν θεοῦ; θεὸς ὁ δικαιῶν· τίς ὁ κατακρινῶν; the last clause opens verse 34.
New lemma: Ἀλήθειαν λέγω ἐν Χριστῷ, οὐ ψεύδομαι, συμμαρτυρούσης μοι τῆς συνειδήσεώς μου (Cyril stops before ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ); repeated in shorter form with καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς.
πρωτότοκον αὐτὸν ἀπεκάλει echoes LXX Υἱὸς πρωτότοκός μου Ισραηλ.
Alluded to first (ἀνάθεμα θέλειν εἶναι ἀπὸ Χριστοῦ), then quoted: ηὐχόμην γὰρ ἀνάθεμα εἶναι αὐτὸς ἐγὼ ἀπὸ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ὑπὲρ τῶν ἀδελφῶν μου.
οὐ γὰρ ἔκρινά τι εἰδέναι ἐν ὑμῖν εἰ μὴ Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν καὶ τοῦτον ἐσταυρωμένον.
τίς ἡμᾶς χωρίσει ἀπὸ τῆς ἀγάπης τοῦ Χριστοῦ; θλῖψις ἢ στενοχωρία ἢ διωγμὸς ἢ λιμὸς ἢ γυμνότης ἢ κίνδυνος ἢ μάχαιρα;

choices.why: οἰκονομικῶς: “with a wise purpose” (with pastoral design, by way of the economy); Θεοῦ κατανεύοντος: “as God grants it”.
κυριοκτόνοι: Cyril's own polemical term, “slayers of the Lord”, translated as it stands, not softened or sharpened.

λειτουργὸς τῶν θείων εὐαγγελίων: the plural εὐαγγέλια rendered “the divine gospel” (the message, not the four books); possible echo of Romans 15:16 (λειτουργὸν Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ εἰς τὰ ἔθνη), not cited inline because the wording differs.

choices.term: μᾶλλον δὲ τῆς ἀγάπης τὴν πλήρωσιν ἔχει
choices.english: or rather, it is the fullness of love
choices.why: μᾶλλον δὲ τῆς ἀγάπης τὴν πλήρωσιν ἔχει: “or rather, it is the fullness of love”; not cited as Romans 13:10, whose wording (πλήρωμα νόμου ἡ ἀγάπη) and sense differ.

choices.term: ἑτέροις γεμὴν τὸ χρῆμα ἐνεῖναι ἑλεῖν
choices.english: while choosing that others should have it
choices.why: ἑτέροις γεμὴν τὸ χρῆμα ἐνεῖναι ἑλεῖν: τὸ χρῆμα (“the thing”) refers back to τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ζωήν; rendered “while choosing that others should have it”.

choices.english: his own salvation as the price of the salvation of the Jews
choices.why: τὴν ἑαυτοῦ (sc. σωτηρίαν) as ἀντάλλαγμα: “his own salvation as the price of the salvation of the Jews”.
ηὐχόμην rendered “I could wish”, the usual English for the imperfect in Romans 9:3.

pass_a_gloss: [completes sentence from u07-rem-mid: he who did not spare the Son by nature, that he might save those in danger and] free (ἀπαλλάξῃ) from dangers (κινδύνων), how not also with him will he grant (χαριεῖται) us all things? Who will accuse (ἐγκαλέσει) against the chosen (ἐκλεκτῶν) of God? God the one justifying (δικαιῶν), who the one condemning (κατακρίνων)? Perhaps (τάχα) also economically (οἰκονομικῶς) Paul does not let the mind of the called fall into helplessness (ἀμηχανίαν), but teaches that from the ancient (ἀρχαίων) sins they will be freed (ἐλευθερωθήσονται), and will be justified, God assenting (κατανεύοντος). For if also every sin has transgression (παράβασιν) of the divine law and condemns the one being careless (ῥαθυμοῦντα), yet if the Lord of the law himself pardons (συγχωρεῖ), who the one condemning the one who has sinned? Truth I speak in Christ, I do not lie, my conscience (συνειδήσεως) bearing witness with (συμμαρτυρούσης) me. Chosen-out (ἀπόλεκτον) God made Israel in the beginnings, and indeed also called him firstborn (πρωτότοκον); but they became boasters (ἀλαζόνες) and insolent (ὑβρισταί), and what is still beyond these, Lord-killers (κυριοκτόνοι); for this reason (ταύτῃτοι) they have perished (διολώλασι), for they became sent away (ἀπόπεμπτοι) and cast out (ἐξεῤῥιμμένοι), and having slipped (ὠλισθηκότες) entirely from the kinship/closeness (οἰκειότητος) toward God, they have been set behind (κατόπιν) the nations (ἐθνῶν); they have appeared also strangers (ἀλλότριοι) of the hope of the fathers. Since the blessed Paul was set as minister (λειτουργός) of the divine gospels, and was proclaiming (διεκήρυττε) Jesus to the nations, up and down (ἄνω τε καὶ κάτω) saying those from the blood of Israel had fallen away (ἀποπεπτωκέναι), and strongly affirming (διισχυριζόμενος) that those once in darkness (σκότῳ) and servants (θεραπευτάς) of demons became called according to purpose and foreknowledge of God, so that some of the more ignorant (ἀμαθεστέρων) might not think him all but (μονονουχί) to leap upon (ἐνάλλεσθαι) those of his race (ἐκ γένους) lying down, and to smile upon (ἐπιμειδιᾶν) the fallen, he makes the defense (ἀπολογίαν) necessary and says: truth I speak in Christ, I do not lie, and the rest. But over those who have gone out (ἐκπεφοιτηκόσιν) to this of perversity (σκαιότητος), so as to slip from the love toward God, and to endure (ἀνατλῆναι) harsh penalties (δίκας) for this thereafter, one might be gloomy (ἐπιστυγνάσειεν); and to drip (ἐπιστάξαι) a tear for them from mutual love (φιλαλληλίας) would be not beyond reason (λόγου), rather it has the fulfilment (πλήρωσιν) of love; but indeed also on behalf of them to wish to be anathema (ἀνάθεμα) from Christ, beyond the measures (μέτρων) of love then; for one would not choose (ἕλοιτο), if he is in good mind (ἐν καλῷ φρενός), for the sake of the salvation (σωτηρίας) of others to offend (προσκρούειν) God, and to make his own life as nothing, but choose (ἑλεῖν) the thing to be in others. What then does he say, setting forth (προτιθείς) his own as exchange (ἀντάλλαγμα) for the salvation of the Jews? Therefore hyperbolic (ὑπερβολικός) the word, and has proof (ἀπόδειξιν) of the most perfect (τελεωτάτης) love; for I was wishing/praying (ηὐχόμην), he says, to be anathema myself from the Christ on behalf of my brothers; for it is like as if he says: if, I having offended Christ, Israel is saved (ἀνασώζεται), I myself would have chosen (εἱλόμην ἄν); he who also to those justified in faith said: for I judged (ἔκρινα) to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ and him crucified; he who proclaims to all: who will separate (χωρίσει) us from the love of Christ? affliction (θλῖψις) or distress (στενοχωρία) or persecution (διωγμός) or famine or nakedness or danger or sword? to undergo (ὑποστῆναι) so terrible an evil, and one on behalf of [continues in u08-open: all to go to destruction].
pass_b_english: …set them free from dangers, how will he not also, with him, give us all things (Romans 8:32)? “Who will bring a charge against God’s chosen? It is God who justifies; who is the one who condemns?” (Romans 8:33–34). Perhaps Paul, with a wise purpose, does not let the minds of the called fall into helplessness, but teaches that they will be set free from their former sins and will be justified, as God grants it. For although every sin involves a transgression of the divine law and condemns the careless, yet if the Lord of the law himself forgives, who is the one who condemns the sinner?

“I am speaking the truth in Christ, I am not lying; my conscience bears witness with me” (Romans 9:1). In the beginning God made Israel his chosen one and even called him firstborn (Exodus 4:22). But they became boastful and insolent, and, what goes beyond even this, slayers of the Lord. That is why they have perished; for they have been sent away and cast out, and, having slipped wholly from their closeness to God, they have been placed behind the nations; and they have shown themselves strangers to the hope of the fathers.

Now the blessed Paul had been appointed a minister of the divine gospel and was proclaiming Jesus to the nations. Again and again he said that those of Israel’s blood had fallen away, and he insisted that those who were once in darkness and served demons had become called according to the purpose and foreknowledge of God. So that none of the less instructed might think he was all but leaping on his own kin as they lay fallen, and smiling over their fall, he makes a necessary defense and says, “I am speaking the truth in Christ, I am not lying,” and what follows (Romans 9:1).

Over those who have gone so far in perversity as to slip from their love for God, and then to suffer harsh penalties for it, one might well grieve; and to shed a tear for them out of fellow feeling would not be beyond reason; or rather, it is the fullness of love. But to wish even to be accursed from Christ on their behalf (Romans 9:3) goes beyond the measures of love. For no one, if he is in his right mind, would choose to offend God for the sake of the salvation of others, counting his own life as nothing while choosing that others should have it.

What, then, does he mean in putting forward his own salvation as the price of the salvation of the Jews? The statement is a hyperbole, and it gives proof of the most perfect love. “For I could wish,” he says, “that I myself were accursed from Christ for the sake of my brothers” (Romans 9:3). It is as if he were saying, “If Israel were saved by my offending Christ, I myself would have chosen it.” He who said to those justified in faith, “For I decided to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and him crucified” (1 Corinthians 2:2); he who proclaims to all, “Who will separate us from the love of Christ? Will affliction, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or danger, or sword?” (Romans 8:35): to undergo so dreadful an evil, and one on behalf of…

ἀπαλλάξῃ κινδύνων, πῶς οὐχὶ καὶ σὺν αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα ἡμῖν χαριεῖται; Τίς ἐγκαλέσει
κατὰ ἐκλεκτῶν Θεοῦ; Θεὸς ὁ δικαιῶν, τίς ὁ κατακρίνων; Τάχα δὲ καὶ οἰκονομικῶς ὁ
Παῦλος οὐκ ἐᾷ τὸν νοῦν τῶν κεκλημένων εἰς ἀμηχανίαν ἐμπεσεῖν, ἀλλὰ διδάσκει ὅτι
τῶν μὲν ἀρχαίων ἁμαρτιῶν ἐλευθερωθήσονται, δικαιωθήσονται δὲ, Θεοῦ
κατανεύοντος. εἰ γὰρ καὶ πᾶσα ἁμαρτία τοῦ θείου νόμου παράβασιν ἔχει καὶ κατακρίνει
τὸν ῥαθυμοῦντα, ἀλλ' εἰ καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ τοῦ νόμου Κύριος συγχωρεῖ, τίς ὁ κατακρίνων τὸν
ἡμαρτηκότα; 223 Ἀλήθειαν λέγω ἐν Χριστῷ, οὐ ψεύδομαι, συμμαρτυρούσης μοι τῆς
συνειδήσεώς μου. Ἀπόλεκτον μὲν ἐποιεῖτο Θεὸς ἐν ἀρχαῖς τὸν Ἰσραὴλ, καὶ δὴ καὶ
πρωτότοκον αὐτὸν ἀπεκάλει· ἀλλὰ γεγόνασιν ἀλαζόνες καὶ ὑβρισταὶ, καὶ τὸ ἔτι τούτων
ἐπέκεινα κυριοκτόνοι· ταύτῃτοι διολώλασι, γεγόνασι γὰρ ἀπόπεμπτοι καὶ ἐξεῤῥιμμένοι,
καὶ τῆς πρὸς Θεὸν οἰκειότητος εἰς ἅπαν ὠλισθηκότες, τέθεινται κατόπιν ἐθνῶν·
πεφήνασι δὲ καὶ τῆς τῶν πατέρων ἐλπίδος ἀλλότριοι. ἐπειδὴ δὲ ὁ μακάριος Παῦλος τῶν
θείων εὐαγγελίων τέθειται λειτουργὸς, καὶ διεκήρυττε τοῖς ἔθνεσιν τὸν Ἰησοῦν, ἄνω τε
καὶ κάτω τοὺς ἐξ αἵματος Ἰσραὴλ ἀποπεπτωκέναι λέγων, καὶ τοὺς ἐν σκότῳ ποτὲ καὶ
τῶν δαιμονίων θεραπευτὰς κλητοὺς γενέσθαι κατὰ πρόθεσιν καὶ πρόγνωσιν Θεοῦ
διισχυριζόμενος, ἵνα μή τινες οἴωνται τῶν ἀμαθεστέρων μονονουχὶ κειμένοις καὶ
ἐνάλλεσθαι τοῖς ἐκ γένους αὐτὸν, καὶ πεσοῦσιν ἐπιμειδιᾶν, ἀναγκαίαν ποιεῖται τὴν
ἀπολογίαν καί φησιν Ἀλήθειαν λέγω ἐν Χριστῷ, οὐ ψεύδομαι, καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς. ἀλλὰ τοῖς
μὲν εἰς τοῦτο σκαιότητος ἐκπεφοιτηκόσιν, ὡς τῆς εἰς Θεὸν ἀγάπης ἀπολισθεῖν, σκληράς
τε τὰς ἐπὶ τούτῳ λοιπὸν ἀνατλῆναι δίκας, ἐπιστυγνάσειεν ἄν τις· καὶ τὸ ἐκ φιλαλληλίας
αὐτοῖς ἐπιστάξαι δάκρυον εἴη ἂν οὐ πέρα λόγου, μᾶλλον δὲ τῆς ἀγάπης τὴν πλήρωσιν
ἔχει· τό γε δὴ καὶ ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν ἀνάθεμα θέλειν εἶναι ἀπὸ Χριστοῦ, μέτρων ἐπέκεινα τῶν
ἀγάπης λοιπόν· οὐ γὰρ ἂν ἕλοιτό τις εἴπερ ἐστὶν ἐν καλῷ φρενὸς, τῆς ἑτέρων ἕνεκα
σωτηρίας προσκρούειν Θεῷ, καὶ ποιεῖσθαι μὲν παρ' οὐδὲν τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ζωὴν, ἑτέροις
γεμὴν τὸ χρῆμα ἐνεῖναι ἑλεῖν.
224 Τί οὖν ἄρα φησὶ, τῆς Ἰουδαίων σωτηρίας ἀντάλλαγμα τὴν ἑαυτοῦ προτιθείς;
οὐκοῦν ὑπερβολικὸς ὁ λόγος, καὶ ἀγάπης ἀπόδειξιν ἔχει τῆς τελεωτάτης· ηὐχόμην γάρ
φησιν ἀνάθεμα εἶναι αὐτὸς ἐγὼ ἀπὸ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ὑπὲρ τῶν ἀδελφῶν μου· ὅμοιον γὰρ ὡς

αὐτὸς ἐγώ· ὁ καὶ τοῖς ἐν πίστει δεδικαιωμένοις εἰπών "Οὐ γὰρ ἔκρινά τι "εἰδέναι ἐν
ὑμῖν, εἰ μὴ Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν, καὶ τοῦτον ἐσταυ"ρωμένον," ὁ πᾶσι διακηρύττων "Τίς ἡμᾶς

reviewer: claude (Wave A review, clause by clause against the Greek)
review_notes: Staged translation checked clause by clause; κυριοκτόνοι kept as Cyril's own term, Scripture IDs (Romans 8:32, 8:33–34, 9:1, 9:3, 8:35; Exodus 4:22; 1 Corinthians 2:2) are right, and the unfinished closing sentence is left open with an ellipsis as in the source. Fixed in tr6.json: (1) the γάρ in 'γεγόνασι γὰρ ἀπόπεμπτοι' was dropped ('That is why they have perished. They were sent away'), now 'That is why they have perished; for they have been sent away and cast out'; (2) μᾶλλον δὲ ... τὴν πλήρωσιν ἔχει was a separate stiff sentence 'Rather, it holds the fullness of love', now joined as 'or rather, it is the fullness of love' (translator note updated).
Copy-text: PG 74; Fragmenta in Romanos via Khazarzar (Fragmenta in sancti Pauli epistulam ad Romanos.pdf).

The row opens mid-sentence: ἀπαλλάξῃ κινδύνων completes ἵνα σώσῃ κινδυνεύοντας, καί from u07-rem-mid, so the English opens with an ellipsis. It ends mid-sentence at καὶ εἷς ὑπέρ; the phrase continues in u08-open (πάντων χωρῆσαι πρὸς ὄλεθρον). The long sentence has no finite main verb in the source; the closing infinitives are kept as they stand and nothing is supplied.
οἰκονομικῶς: “with a wise purpose” (with pastoral design, by way of the economy); Θεοῦ κατανεύοντος: “as God grants it”.
ὁ τοῦ νόμου Κύριος: God as Lord of the law; capitalised.
κυριοκτόνοι: Cyril's own polemical term, “slayers of the Lord”, translated as it stands, not softened or sharpened.

λειτουργὸς τῶν θείων εὐαγγελίων: the plural εὐαγγέλια rendered “the divine gospel” (the message, not the four books); possible echo of Romans 15:16 (λειτουργὸν Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ εἰς τὰ ἔθνη), not cited inline because the wording differs.
τοὺς ἐν σκότῳ ποτέ: possible echo of Ephesians 5:8 (ἦτε γάρ ποτε σκότος); not cited inline because the wording differs.
μᾶλλον δὲ τῆς ἀγάπης τὴν πλήρωσιν ἔχει: “or rather, it is the fullness of love”; not cited as Romans 13:10, whose wording (πλήρωμα νόμου ἡ ἀγάπη) and sense differ.
ἑτέροις γεμὴν τὸ χρῆμα ἐνεῖναι ἑλεῖν: τὸ χρῆμα (“the thing”) refers back to τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ζωήν; rendered “while choosing that others should have it”.
τὴν ἑαυτοῦ (sc. σωτηρίαν) as ἀντάλλαγμα: “his own salvation as the price of the salvation of the Jews”.
ηὐχόμην rendered “I could wish”, the usual English for the imperfect in Romans 9:3.
PG column numbers 223 and 224 and the page number 21 are dropped from the reading text.
